title: Masked directed codebook margin with a relational codebook term
equation: A[b,c] = ||z_src[b] - E[c]||_1 ; B[b,c] = ||z_tgt[b] - E[c]||_1 ; c*_src = argmin_c A[b,c] ; c*_tgt = argmin_c B[b,c] ; r[b] = max(0, margin + B[b,c*_tgt] - A[b,c*_src]) ; p[b] = softmax_c(-A[b,c]/temperature) ; q[b] = softmax_c(-B[b,c]/temperature) ; G[i,j] = ||E[i] - E[j]||_1 ; s[b] = sum_{i,j} p[b,i] q[b,j] G[i,j] ; L = sum_b mask[b] (r[b] + structural_weight * s[b]) / sum_b mask[b]

symbols.z_src: the source residual of the pair, [B, D]
symbols.z_tgt: the target residual of the pair, [B, D]
symbols.mask: 1 for a valid pair, 0 for an invalid one, [B]

hypotheses: Holding the level-0 codebook entry of the target closer to the target than the source's entry is to the source pushes the encoder to separate the two items in the level-0 code, which is where the SID's first token is decided.

Comparing the two codebook assignments through the codebook's own pairwise geometry adds a term that is sensitive to the RELATION between the two assignments rather than to their distance, so it should not collapse when one level-0 entry dominates.
expected_failure_modes: the margin term's clamp makes the gradient vanish once the target is closer than the source, so the term can sit at zero and contribute nothing
the argmin is a discrete selection, so the loss is not differentiable at a tie and a finite-difference check at such a point measures a jump
the relational term is symmetric under exchanging the two assignments, so the directional content of the mechanism comes from the margin term alone
the codebook path can be silently detached, leaving the encoder to learn a term the codebook cannot see

tests.statement: swapping the source and the target changes the loss: the mechanism is a directed transition, not a similarity
permuting the codebook rows leaves the loss unchanged
a masked pair contributes nothing and the denominator counts only the valid pairs
the loss is finite at a tie in the argmin, on identical codebook rows, and when every pair is masked out
the gradient reaches the source residual, the target residual and the level-0 codebook

forbidden_substitutions.why: the specification declares nonzero gradient targets on the source residual, the target residual and the codebook; a detach anywhere in the mechanism silently cuts one of them off

the relational term is a discrepancy between two codebook assignments measured through the codebook's own geometry; a per-element mean squared error is a different quantity that happens to be computable
the mechanism is directed: the source and the target play different roles, and averaging the two directions would make it a similarity rather than a transition

provenance.authored_by: main agent (issue #102, the reference mechanism of the MVG programme)
provenance.review: the frozen specification was written first and the independent reference implementation was written from the equation; the judges compare the production module with that reference on the forward value and on the intermediates
